quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid serious injury?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips less than five miles long, just a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Encourage them to take less-crowded roads.
Encourage friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: What percentage of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It supplies about 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Ride in the center of the lane so you appear in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before you leave. Have them get on after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: How long should a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: You do not need to do it before every ride.

questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. A complete inspection usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep a steady speed or accelerate gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to stabilize your suspension. Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually through the turn.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Ride in the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as soon as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to be farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly move up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Move into the part of your lane that will bring you into an oncoming driver's view as early as possible. For example, when approaching a blind corner to your right, move to the left portion of your lane to be seen sooner.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid hitting the animal.
Change lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: In traffic, stay in your lane even if a small animal is in the road. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another car. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle rider check their mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch for hazards behind you.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep the bike straight. Brake slowly on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: A thorough check of your motorcycle:

options.text: Only a mechanic can do it properly.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should be done only after a ride.
Can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find problems that could be dangerous.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should avoid riding in pairs because:

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Light reflecting off helmets may make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
Riders on the left side cannot exit a highway easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in pairs. Each rider needs enough space to move around and avoid dangers.

questions.question: Which of the following best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Eyeglasses, sunglasses, and most windshields do not.

questions.question: Which of the following gives a rider the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. Windshields and eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, all of the following are hazards, except:
questions.explanation: Watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects that may be thrown from it. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: Which of the following surfaces gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates in the road all have poor traction. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of riding experience. Most crashes happen in daylight at low speeds.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Stay farther away from other vehicles.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Use your high beam headlight except when you are following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane.

questions.explanation: Many surfaces can make it hard for tires to grip the road. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: Which formation keeps riders in a group closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group to stay close together while keeping safe space around each rider. Use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, what is best?

options.text: One rider must finish passing before the next rider starts to pass.
Several riders can pass the vehicle at the same time.
The last rider should wave to signal no more motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider must finish passing before the next rider starts to pass.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should pass one at a time. Each rider should finish passing and return to their place in the formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no damage, such as cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is okay if traffic is heavy.
Is okay during the day to reduce traffic.
Is okay if the rider feels comfortable.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, it is illegal for motorcycles and mopeds to pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to daytime, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Leave more space between you and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights ahead to see farther. Always be ready to change your position in the lane, especially at night.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Be ready to move to a different lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers can see you as easily as they see other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about being seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, making them hard to see. For safety, ride defensively and assume that other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: When you are ready to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Not signal so you do not distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal first and check for traffic. Pass safely, then signal and move back to your original lane when it is safe.
